newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais, Amex in corporate card deal.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais, Amex in corporate card deal.

text.p: French bank Credit Lyonnais and American Express said on Wednesday that they had signed a deal under which the French bank will offer corporate clients a payment card to pay business expenses.

The card, to be known as Carte Entreprise, will bear the names of Credit Lyonnais and American Express and will be available during the second quarter of 1997, Credit Lyonnais and American Express said in a joint statement.
"It is the first time we have issued a co-branded card with a French bank," said a spokeswoman for American Express.
The only other European bank with which American Express has struck a similar deal is the British bank, National Westminster Plc, she said.
The agreement is a major step for the U.S. travel and financial services giant which has, since 1996, been seeking partner banks to boost its presence in major global markets.
The agreement is "part of our new strategy to open up the network of our establishment to other partners and have co-branded cards," the spokeswoman said.
American Express has signed agreements with other European banks but they involve distribution of American Express cards, not the issuing of co-branded cards.
Credit Lyonnais said the move showed its determination to "base its marketing policy on satisfying client needs".
